hosts.browser: headless Google Chrome, OfflineAudioContext — all 18 kind/rate results pass (delayonly, fanout, fanin error 0)
hosts.ios: iPhone 17 Pro simulator, iOS 26.5, RN 0.86.3, RN Audio API 0.13.3, Release; three launches
hosts.android: emulator dosekeep_api35 (API 35, arm64-v8a), same versions, Release APK; three launches

delayonly.expected: impulse value 1 at frame D (441 @44.1 kHz, 480 @48 kHz)
delayonly.native: impulse value 1 at frame 0 on every launch, both platforms, both rates
delayonly.reading: DelayNode applies zero delay in the native OfflineAudioContext. Deterministic.

fanout.expected: 1.5 at frame 0 (source → gain 1 → destination, source → gain 0.5 → destination)
fanout.reading: Only the path connected last reached the output.

fanin.reading: The destination delivered one input, not the sum.

delay.native: single impulse at frame 0 valued 0.125 or 0.25; repeatError 0.125 on some launches
delay.reading: Consistent with zero delay plus one surviving destination input whose identity varies with graph-event ordering.

convolver.reading: No lag; a 0.2–0.3% scale deficit; residual up to 4.9% of full scale remains after removing scale, identical on all six launches. The native convolver is repeatable but not a sample-exact convolution of the supplied response.

contrast: The fixture-version-2/3 timing fixture fans twelve impulse sources into one GainNode and every impulse arrives on native, so fan-in into a GainNode is not affected. Fan-in into the destination and fan-out from a source toward the destination are.
conclusions: Native OfflineAudioContext DelayNode is unusable for TuneJS effects (zero delay); the feedforward Delay effect and any delay-based binaural cue are browser-only until the host changes.

Multiple connections into engine.output are unsafe on native. TuneJS will own a unity master GainNode as the output host with a single edge to the destination; a fixture-version-6 probe (fan-in and fan-out summed through a GainNode) must pass natively before that is relied on.
Native convolution differs from the browser by up to 4.9% of full scale; reverb output is host-dependent. Offline rendering (Wave 7) must not assume host-convolver equality across platforms.
All findings are OfflineAudioContext measurements on a simulator and an emulator; live AudioContext behavior on devices is unmeasured.
